item.title: 82 Brondesbury Villas NW6 6AD, 1st November
item.description:

He said Brent Council should be notified regarding the mature street tree situated on the public footpath fronting the property. A formal request should be submitted to implement an arboricultural management plan, ideally incorporating a canopy crown reduction of up to two-thirds to curb excessive evapotranspiration and soil moisture depletion.

Advised by truck company it is a unauthorised highway obstruction and safety hazard and that stretching items over a live public road is strictly illegal without a permit.

item.title: Black Path, parallel to West Hampstead Thameslink station, 1st November
item.description:
Dear sir/madam, I live in West Hampstead and there is a local path called the Black Path that runs parallel to the West Hampstead Thameslink station. This path is showing signs of potential soil slippage in various parts. For example, there is evidence of brick walls starting to tilt down the hill as well as some of the path’s asphalt cracking and slipping down the hill. I am therefore concerned that the ground beneath the path could slip further, especially if there are periods of heavy rain in the future. In a worst case scenario, it could slip down onto the Thameslink platforms beneath. There is also the related risk that the tilting walls could collapse onto the path. I would ask that an expert review is the path and the underlying soil stability with urgency. Best, Ewan Macaulay

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Black Path, West Hampstead, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
